'''Boban Marjanović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Бобан Марјановић}}; born August 15, 1988) is a [[Serbia|Serbian]] professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[KK Ilirija|Ilirija]] of the [[Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian League]] and the [[ABA League]]. He represented the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national team]] in international competition.

A 2007 junior world champion, Marjanović played abroad in Russia and Lithuania between 2010 and 2012 before making his breakthrough in his home country. As the 2013 MVP of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian league]], he moved to [[KK Crvena zvezda]], with whom he won the national championship and the cross-border [[Adriatic Basketball League]] (ABA League) in 2015. In addition to further MVP awards in Serbia, Marjanović was also voted one of the five best players in the ABA League and the top European club competition [[EuroLeague]] in 2015.

Marjanović signed his first ever [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] contract as a 27-year-old rookie in 2015 with the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He also played for the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Philadelphia 76ers]], [[Dallas Mavericks]] and [[Houston Rockets]] between 2016 and 2024. At {{cvt|2.24|m|ftin}}, Marjanović is one of the [[List of tallest players in NBA history|tallest players in NBA history]].  
{{Toclimit|3}}

==Early life==
Marjanović was born and raised in [[Boljevac]] in eastern Serbia. Although he was tall from a young age, his family members are all of average height: his father stands only {{height|ft=5|in=9}} in height.<ref>{{Cite magazine|first=Tim|last=Rogers|title=Boban The Great |url=https://www.dmagazine.com/publications/d-magazine/2020/may/boban-marjanovic-dallas-mavericks/|magazine=D Magazine|date=May 13, 2020}}</ref> A [[Pituitary disease|pituitary gland condition]] is thought to have contributed to his [[gigantism]].<ref name="height">{{cite news |last1=Nuamah |first1=Charles |title=Tall NBA Players Who Had Relatively Short Parents |url=https://howtheyplay.com/team-sports/Tall-NBA-Players-With-or-Who-Had-Relatively-Short-Parents |access-date=August 20, 2020|website=How They Play|date=June 18, 2020}}</ref>

Marjanović began playing basketball with the youth teams of Boljevac-based club [[KK Rtanj|Rtanj]].<ref name=youthint>{{Cite news|title=Boban Marjanović i mit o pradedinom opanku|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html:431901-Boban-Marjanovic-i-mit-o-pradedinom-opanku|access-date=September 30, 2015|newspaper=[[Večernje novosti]]|date=May 2, 2013|language=sr}}</ref> By age 14, he was {{height|m=2.09}} tall, and began playing for the Serbian professional team [[KK Vršac|Hemofarm]].<ref name=youthint/> He played in their youth categories until the 2005–06 season.

==Professional career==
===Early career===
Marjanović joined Hemofarm's first team, playing in the [[ABA League|Adriatic League]], in the second half of the 2005–06 season. He played there until January 2007 when he moved to the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] team [[KK Radnički Kragujevac (2009–2014)|Swisslion Takovo]] on loan. After half seasons there, Marjanović returned to Hemofarm. His teammates included [[Stefan Marković (basketball)|Stefan Marković]] and [[Milan Mačvan]], with whom he had played on the Serbian junior national team.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

In summer 2010, Marjanović signed a three-year contract with [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], on the insistence of [[Duško Vujošević]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73477/cska-moscow-adds-size-with-marjanovic|url-status=dead|title=CSKA Moscow adds size with Marjanovic|website=euroleague.net | date=July 6, 2010 | access-date=February 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151022001353/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/73477/cska-moscow-adds-size-with-marjanovic|archive-date=October 22, 2015}}</ref> After Vujošević was sacked, Marjanović lost his place in CSKA's first team. On December 31, 2010, he moved to [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris]] on loan until the end of the 2010–11 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2010-11-signings/i/80976/4465/zalgiris-gets-center-marjanovic-on-loan-from-cska |title=ZALGIRIS gets center Marjanovic on loan |website=euroleague.net |date=December 31, 2010|access-date=February 22, 2013|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615182745/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2010-11-signings/i/80976/4465/zalgiris-gets-center-marjanovic-on-loan-from-cska |archive-date=June 15, 2011}}</ref> In July 2011, Marjanović signed for [[BC Nizhny Novgorod|Nizhny Novgorod]],<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/russia/87020/boban-marjanovic-moves-to-bc-nizhny-novgorod.html|url-status=dead|title=Boban Marjanovic moves to BC Nizhny Novgorod | website=sportando.net|date=July 2, 2011 | access-date=February 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919174855/https://sportando.com/en/europe/russia/87020/boban-marjanovic-moves-to-bc-nizhny-novgorod.html|archive-date=September 19, 2015}}</ref> staying there for half a season.

===Return to Serbia===
In January 2012, Marjanović returned to Serbia and signed for [[KK Radnički Kragujevac (2009–2014)|Radnički Kragujevac]] on loan for the rest of the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/boban-marjanovic-pojacao-radnicki-iz-kragujevca/tf6qq0g|url-status=dead|title=Boban Marjanović pojačao Radnički iz Kragujevca | language=sr | website=Blic | date=January 7, 2012|access-date=February 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160103062726/https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/boban-marjanovic-pojacao-radnicki-iz-kragujevca/tf6qq0g|archive-date=January 3, 2016}}</ref> The same year in July, Marjanović signed a contract with Serbian team [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Vizura]] for the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/other-leagues/93726/boban-marjanovic-inks-with-mega-vizura.html|title=Boban Marjanovic inks with Mega Vizura|website=sportando.net | date=July 20, 2012 | access-date=February 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919202959/https://sportando.com/en/europe/other-leagues/93726/boban-marjanovic-inks-with-mega-vizura.html|archive-date=September 19, 2015}}</ref> He was named the [[BLS Super League MVP|MVP of the Serbian League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sport.blic.rs/Kosarka/Domaca-kosarka-i-ABA/233826/Boban-Marjanovic-MVP-Superlige-Rakocevic-drugi-Bakic-treci|url-status=dead|title=Boban Marjanović MVP Superlige, Rakočević drugi, Bakić treći|language=sr|website=Blic|access-date=July 2, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608074546/http://sport.blic.rs/Kosarka/Domaca-kosarka-i-ABA/233826/Boban-Marjanovic-MVP-Superlige-Rakocevic-drugi-Bakic-treci|archive-date=June 8, 2013}}</ref>

====Crvena zvezda (2013–2015)====
[[File:BobanMarjanovic.JPG|thumb|175px|Marjanović playing for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] during the 2014–15 season]]
On July 2, 2013, Marjanović signed a two-year contract with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/102882/red-star-adds-size-with-boban-marjanovic.html|title=Red Star adds size with Boban Marjanovic |website=Sportando|date=July 2, 2013|access-date=July 2, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220171439/http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/102882/red-star-adds-size-with-boban-marjanovic.html|archive-date=December 20, 2016|url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Marjanović dve godine u Zvezdi!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2013&mm=07&dd=02&nav_id=728527|website=B92|date=February 7, 2013|access-date=July 2, 2013|language=sr}}</ref> In December 2013, he was named [[EuroLeague MVP of the Round|EuroLeague MVP of the Round for Round 10]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Regular season Round 10 bwin MVP: Boban Marjanovic, Crvena Zvezda Telekom|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/126938/180|access-date=April 2, 2014|website=Euroleague|date=December 21, 2013}}</ref> In April 2014, along with his teammate [[DeMarcus Nelson]], he was selected for [[ABA League Ideal Starting Five|the Ideal Team]] for the [[2013–14 ABA League]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=The ideal five of the 2013/14 season selected|url=http://www.abaliga.com/a7487/News/The_ideal_five_of_the_2013/14_season_selected.html|website=ABA League|access-date=April 21, 2014|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://archive.today/20140421084230/http://www.abaliga.com/a7487/News/The_ideal_five_of_the_2013/14_season_selected.html|archive-date=April 21, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=ABA: 'Večiti' i Šarić u timu lige|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=04&dd=21&nav_id=838871|website=[[B92]]|date=April 21, 2014 |access-date=April 21, 2014|language=sr}}</ref>

In the first match of the [[2014–15 Euroleague]] on October 18, 2014, Marjanović led his team to a 76–68 victory against [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]], scoring 22 points and pulling down 10 rebounds in 28 minutes on the court.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Crvena Zvezda takes first Game of the Week against Galatasaray|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=10&pcode=LMG&seasoncode=E2014#!report|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|access-date=October 18, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150629184210/http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=10&pcode=LMG&seasoncode=E2014#!report#!report|archive-date=June 29, 2015}}</ref> He was later named the EuroLeague MVP of the Round for Round 1.<ref>{{cite news|title=Regular season Round 1 bwin MVP: Boban Marjanovic, Crvena Zvezda Telekom Belgrade|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/142316/180|date=October 18, 2014|access-date=October 18, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141231223504/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/142316/180|archive-date=December 31, 2014}}</ref> On November 22, Marjanović recorded 23 points and a career-high 17 rebounds for a [[Performance Index Rating|total index rating]] of 39 in a double overtime 103–110 loss against Galatasaray.<ref>{{Cite web|title=EL: Erceg ukrao pobedu Zvezdi!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2014&mm=11&dd=21&nav_id=926813|website=B92|date=November 21, 2014|access-date=June 28, 2026|language=sr}}</ref> At the time, his 17 rebounds in a single game was the highest number by any player in the EuroLeague since 2011–12.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Erceg, Arroyo star in Galatasaray's 2OT win over Crvena Zvezda|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=70&pcode=DHF&seasoncode=E2014#!report|url-status=dead|access-date=November 21, 2014|website=Euroleague|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129044709/http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=70&pcode=DHF&seasoncode=E2014#!report|archive-date=November 29, 2014}}</ref>

In a match against [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] on April 9, he set the [[EuroLeague records|EuroLeague record]] (since the 2000–01 season) for the most rebounds in a single season with 256, passing the previous record by [[Mirsad Türkcan]], who had 248 rebounds in the [[2002–03 Euroleague|2002–03]] season.<ref name=euromilestone>{{Cite web|title=Zvezda's Marjanovic sets rebounds mark to end milestone season|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5vk5m9esb588vye5|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|date=April 9, 2015|access-date=April 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305212254/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5vk5m9esb588vye5|archive-date=March 5, 2016}}</ref> He also set the EuroLeague record for the most [[Double-double|double-doubles]] in a season with 16, surpassing the record of 14 set by [[Tanoka Beard]] in the [[2004–05 Euroleague|2004–05]] season.<ref name=euromilestone/> Over 24 EuroLeague matches, his all career-highs were 16.6 points on average, a league-leading 10.7 rebounds and a record (since the EuroLeague 2000–01 season) of 25.67 in [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]].<ref name=euromilestone/><ref>{{cite news|title=Marjanović u istoriji Evrolige!|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2015&mm=04&dd=09&nav_id=979123|website=B92|date=April 9, 2015|access-date=April 10, 2015|language=sr}}</ref>

On April 2, 2015, he was selected for [[ABA League Ideal Starting Five|the Ideal Team]] for the 2014–15 ABA League season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marjanović heads the ideal five |url=http://www.abaliga.com/a9653/News/Marjanovic_heads_the_ideal_five.html |access-date=May 9, 2015|website=ABA League|date=April 2, 2015|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150404172555/http://www.abaliga.com/a9653/News/Marjanovic_heads_the_ideal_five.html |archive-date=April 4, 2015}}</ref> Later that month, he helped his team to win the [[2014–15 ABA League]] trophy.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Crvena zvezda is the new ABA League champion!|url=http://www.abaliga.com/a9839/News/_Crvena_zvezda_is_the_new_ABA_League_champion_.html|website=ABA Liga|access-date=May 6, 2015|date=April 30, 2015 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150710215548/http://www.abaliga.com/a9839/News/_Crvena_zvezda_is_the_new_ABA_League_champion_.html |archive-date=July 10, 2015 }}</ref> He was named the [[ABA League Finals MVP|MVP of the ABA League playoffs]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The MVP is... Boban Marjanović! |url=http://www.abaliga.com/a9840/News/The_MVP_is..._Boban_Marjanovic_.html |access-date=May 6, 2015|website=ABA Liga|date=April 30, 2015|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150501093540/http://www.abaliga.com/a9840/News/The_MVP_is..._Boban_Marjanovic_.html|archive-date=May 1, 2015}}</ref> In May 2015, he was chosen for the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]].<ref>{{cite news|title=All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8|website=Euroleague|date=May 8, 2015|access-date=May 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304135925/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8|archive-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref>

On June 5, 2015, Marjanović was named the [[BLS Super League MVP|Serbian Super League MVP]] for the third consecutive season, having helped his team to reach first place in the regular season with a record of 13–1.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bobi Marjanović – MVP, Nikola Jokić, najefikasniji|url=http://kls.rs/vest.php?id=1694|access-date=June 5, 2015|publisher=KLS|date=June 5, 2015|language=sr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001943/http://kls.rs/vest.php?id=1694|archive-date=March 4, 2016}}</ref> Crvena zvezda won the [[2014–15 Basketball League of Serbia|2014–15 Serbian League]] championship after a 3–0 victory against [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]].<ref>{{Cite web|title='Delije' dočekale: Košarkaši Zvezde šampioni Srbije posle 17 godina!|url=http://sport.blic.rs/Kosarka/Domaca-kosarka-i-ABA/274309/Delije-docekale-Kosarkasi-Zvezde-sampioni-Srbije-posle-17-godina|access-date=June 20, 2015|website=Blic|date=June 18, 2015|language=sr}}</ref>

===San Antonio Spurs (2015–2016)===

in the Spurs' 102–75 win over the [[2015–16 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=October 31, 2015 |title=Leonard, Duncan lead Spurs to 102-75 win over Nets ===Detroit Pistons (2016–2018)===
After the 2015–16 season, Marjanović became a [[NBA salary cap#Restricted free agent|restricted free agent]]. On July 7, 2016, he received a three-year, $21 million offer sheet from the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web |date=July 7, 2016 |title=Boban Marjanovic signs three-year offer sheet with Pistons |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/16857694|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=April 6, 2024}}</ref> The Spurs declined to match the offer<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 11, 2016 |title=Monday's Pistons Links: Boban Marjanovic joins Pistons after Spurs decline to match offer sheet |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nba/post/_/id/22027/mondays-pistons-links-boban-marjanovic-joins-pistons-after-spurs-decline-to-match-offer-sheet|publisher=ESPN|access-date=September 17, 2024}}</ref> and he signed with the Pistons on July 12.<ref>{{cite web |date=July 12, 2016 |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Free Agent Boban Marjanovic |url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-free-agent-boban-marjanovic|publisher=NBA|access-date=April 6, 2024}}</ref> On January 5, 2017, Marjanović recorded 15 points and a career-high 19 rebounds in a 115–114 win over the [[2016–17 Charlotte Hornets season|Charlotte Hornets]]. He had played only 76 minutes all season prior to the game against the Hornets but, with [[Andre Drummond]] in foul trouble and [[Aron Baynes]] out injured, coach [[Stan Van Gundy]] was forced to give Marjanović extended minutes.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 5, 2017 |title=Pistons hold off Hornets when Belinelli's shot is too late |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899959|publisher=ESPN|access-date=April 6, 2024}}</ref> On April 7, 2017, he led the Pistons with a career-high 27 points and 12 rebounds off the bench in a 114–109 win over the [[2016–17 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web |date=April 7, 2017 |title=Johnson hits late 3-pointer, Pistons beat Rockets 114–109 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900560 |access-date=April 6, 2024|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Clippers (2018–2019)===
On January 29, 2018, along with [[Tobias Harris]], [[Avery Bradley]] – a future protected first-round draft pick and a future second-round draft pick – Marjanović was traded to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in exchange for [[Blake Griffin]], [[Willie Reed]] and [[Brice Johnson]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Ibarra |first=Joseph |date=January 29, 2018 |title=Press Release: L.A. Clippers Acquire Harris, Bradley, Marjanović, First & Second-Round Picks |url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/press-release-clippers-acquire-harris-bradley-marjanovic|publisher=NPA|access-date=April 6, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=January 30, 2018 |title=Detroit Pistons acquire Blake Griffin, Willie Reed, Brice Johnson from LA Clippers |url=https://www.nba.com/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-griffin-harris-bradley-marjanovic-release |access-date=April 6, 2024 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> On February 27, 2018, he scored a season-high 18 points in a 122–120 victory against the [[2017–18 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

===Philadelphia 76ers (2019)===
On February 6, 2019, Marjanović, alongside [[Tobias Harris]], was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Seltzer |first=Brian |date=February 6, 2019 |title=Harris, Marjanović, and Scott Acquired From LA Clippers |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/harris-marjanovic-and-scott-acquired-la-clippers|publisher=NBA|access-date=February 6, 2019}}</ref> In 22 appearances for the 76ers in the [[2018–19 Philadelphia 76ers season|regular season]], Marjanović averaged 8.2 points and 5.1 rebounds in 13.9 minutes per game. He later helped the 76ers get past the [[2018–19 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]] in the first round of the [[2019 NBA playoffs]],<ref>{{Cite web|first=Noah|last=Levicj|title=Boban Marjanovic's size is impossible to ignore, but he's more than a novelty |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/boban-marjanovic-size-impossible-ignore-more-than-novelty-nba-playoffs |access-date=May 18, 2019|website=NBC Sports|publisher=NBC|date=April 19, 2019}}</ref> but the 76ers were eventually eliminated by the [[2018–19 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]] in the Conference Semifinals.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Yossi|last=Gossan|title=An early preview of the 2019–20 offseason for the Philadelphia|url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2019/05/16/an-early-preview-of-the-2019-20-offseason-for-the-philadelphia-sixers/ |access-date=May 18, 2019 |website=USA Today|date=May 16, 2019}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2019–2022)===
[[File:Boban Marjanovic (51175591297) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Marjanović with the Mavericks in 2021]]
On July 23, 2019, Marjanović signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Price |first=Dwain |date=July 23, 2019 |title=Mavs sign 76ers free agent center Boban Marjanovic |url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-76ers-free-agent-center-boban-marjanovic |access-date=April 6, 2024 |website=Dalas Mavericks}}</ref> On March 11, 2020, he registered a career-high 31 points, along with 17 rebounds, in a 113–97 win over the [[2019–20 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]], the final game before the [[Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season|season was suspended]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 12, 2020 |title=Mavs avoid 3-game skid with 113-97 win over Nuggets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401161615|publisher=ESPN|access-date=April 6, 2024}}</ref><ref name="nba-suspension-of-season">{{cite press release|title=NBA to suspend season following tonight's games|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=March 11, 2020|url=https://pr.nba.com/nba-to-suspend-season-following-tonights-games/|access-date=March 12, 2020}}</ref> On August 10, 2021, Marjanović re-signed with the Mavericks.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=August 10, 2021 |title=Boban's back! Marjanović re-signs with Mavericks |url=https://www.mavs.com/bobans-back |access-date=April 6, 2024 |work=mavs.com}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2022–2024)===
[[File:1_boban_marjanovic.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Marjanović with the [[Houston Rockets]] in 2023]]
On June 24, 2022, Marjanović was traded alongside [[Trey Burke]], [[Marquese Chriss]], [[Sterling Brown (basketball)|Sterling Brown]] and the draft rights to [[Wendell Moore Jr.]], to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Christian Wood]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks' trade for center Christian Wood is official|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-rockets-trade/|website=Mavs.com|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=June 24, 2022}}</ref> On February 9, 2023, the Rockets waived Marjanović, as a result of a three-team trade.<ref>{{cite web|first=Hiren|last=Joshi|title=Rockets Complete Three-Team Trade with the L.A. Clippers and Memphis Grizzlies|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-three-team-trade-with-the-l-a-clippers-and-memphis-grizzlies|publisher=NBA|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023|quote=In a related move, the Rockets have waived center Boban Marjanović.}}</ref>

However, on February 13, 2023, Marjanović re-signed with the Rockets, four days after being waived.<ref>{{cite web|first=Hiren|last=Joshi|title=Rockets Re-sign Boban Marjanović|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-boban-marjanovic|website=NBA.com|date=September 20, 2023|access-date=September 21, 2023}}</ref> On April 14, 2024, in a road game for the Houston Rockets at the Los Angeles Clippers, the Clippers had a partnership with fast food chain Chick-fil-A, where fans in attendance received a free chicken sandwich if any visiting team misses two consecutive free throws in the 4th quarter of a home game. Marjanović intentionally missed his two free throws, thereby granting those in attendance a free chicken sandwich. The television announcers cried, "He gave them chicken! He's a man of the people!" In September 2024, it was announced he signed at [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahce]] of [[Turkey]].<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=el:Η Φενέρμπαχτσε ανακοίνωσε την απόκτηση του Μπόμπαν Μαριάνοβιτς|url=https://www.sport24.gr/basket/fenermpachtse-metagrafes-anakoinose-tin-apoktisi-toy-mpompan-marianovits.10380464.html|website=Sport24.gr|date=September 18, 2024|access-date=September 18, 2024|language=el}}</ref>

(basketball)|Fenerbahçe Beko]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|BSL]] and the [[EuroLeague]] for the [[2024–25 EuroLeague|2024–25]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Boban Marjanovic Fenerbahçe Beko'da|url=https://fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2024/9/boban-marjanovic-fenerbahce-beko-da|website=Fenerbahce Basketball|date=September 18, 2024|access-date=September 18, 2024|language=tr}}</ref> On December 23, 2024, Marjanović parted ways with the Turkish team, after appearing in 13 games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Boban Marjanovic set to leave Fenerbahce as club explores market |url=https://basketnews.com/news-216798-boban-marjanovic-set-to-leave-fenerbahce-as-club-explores-market.html |access-date=December 23, 2024 |website=Basket News}}</ref>

On December 11, 2025, Marjanović signed with the [[KK Ilirija|Ilirija]] of the [[Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian League]] and the [[ABA League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=After 10 Years Boban Marjanović is Back in ABA, as he Puts on Perspektiva Ilirija Jersey |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/53754/after-10-years-boban-marjanovic-is-back-in-aba-as-he-puts-on-perspektiva-ilirija-jersey |website=ABA Liga|access-date=December 11, 2025 |date=December 11, 2025}}</ref> On May 24, 2026, in the [[Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian League]] game against [[KK Krka|Krka]], Marjanović was involved in a heated verbal exchange with fans of the opposing team, but managed to calm down.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mijailović |first1=Filip |title=Marjanović se zaleteo na navijače, jedva ga zaustavili |url=https://sportklub.n1info.rs/kosarka/ostale-lige-kosarka/boban-marjanovic-hteo-da-tuce-navijace-navijac-ilirija-sasa-doncic/ |access-date=24 July 2026 |work=sportklub.n1info.rs |language=Serbian}}</ref> Over 18 [[2025–26 ABA League First Division|ABA League]] games with Ilirija, he averaged 13.9 points and 8.6 rebounds on 50.0% shooting from the field.

==National team career==
{{see also|2017 Serbia EuroBasket team}}
As a junior national team player of Serbia, Marjanović won gold medals at the [[2007 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] and the [[2008 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]]. He was named on the candidates list before both the [[EuroBasket 2009]] and the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], but did not make the final 12-man squad. His senior debut with the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbian national basketball team]] at a major tournament occurred at [[EuroBasket 2011]] in [[Lithuania]], where Serbia finished in eighth place.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

In August 2015, the San Antonio Spurs prohibited him from playing for the Serbian national team at [[EuroBasket 2015]] due to risk of injury after signs of pain in his left foot, although the [[Basketball Federation of Serbia|Serbian Basketball Federation]] (KSS) stated that no bone fractures were found.<ref>{{cite news|title=Marjanovic Return To National Team Postponed|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_1w8pON5UIsshfP8zWVLZX3.articleMode_on.html|url-status=dead|access-date=August 24, 2015|work=Eurobasket2015.org|date=August 4, 2015|archive-date=October 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002070620/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_1w8pON5UIsshfP8zWVLZX3.articleMode_on.html}}</ref>

Marjanović represented Serbia at [[EuroBasket 2017]]. They won the silver medal, losing the final against [[Slovenia men's national basketball team|Slovenia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Slovenia overcome injuries to claim historic title in Dragic's swansong|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2017/news/slovenia-overcome-injuries-to-claim-historic-title|access-date=September 17, 2017|publisher=FIBA|date=September 17, 2017}}</ref> Over nine tournament games, he earned the average result of 12.4 points, 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game on 56.2% shooting from the field.

At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], the Serbian national team was considered a favorite to win the trophy,<ref>{{Cite web|first=Igor|last=Curkovic|title=FIBA Basketball World Cup Power Rankings|url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/fiba-basketball-world-cup-power-rankings-volume-3 |access-date=September 14, 2019|publisher=FIBA|date=August 28, 2019|volume=3}}</ref> but was eventually upset in the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup final round|quarter-finals]] by [[Argentina men's national basketball team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentina upsets Olympic silver medalist Serbia in FIBA World Cup quarterfinals |url=https://olympics.nbcsports.com/2019/09/10/argentina-serbia-fiba-world-cup/ |access-date=September 14, 2019|website=NBC Sports|date=September 10, 2019}}</ref> With wins over the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] and [[Czech Republic men's national basketball team|Czech Republic]], they finished in fifth place.<ref>{{cite news |title=Serbia defeats USA in FIBA World Cup consolation round play |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/09/12/fiba-world-cup-usa-serbia-game-recap |access-date=September 14, 2019 |publisher=NBA|date=September 12, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bogdanović ponovo briljirao – Srbiji peto mesto u Kini |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kina2019/vesti.php?nav_id=1591176|access-date=September 14, 2019|website=B92|date=September 14, 2019|language=sr}}</ref> Marjanović averaged 6.8 points and 2.5 rebounds over eight matches.

In 2021, Marjanović played the [[Grand master (order)|grand master]] in the 1,629th episode of the Serbian television comedy show ''[[Državni posao]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aGhn7cjiAwE|url-status=live|title=Državni Posao [HQ] – Ep.1629: Veliki majstor (24.06.2021.)|website=[[YouTube]]|date=June 24, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624220513/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aGhn7cjiAwE|archive-date=June 24, 2021}}</ref> Marjanović is close friends with [[Tobias Harris]], with whom he has been traded twice.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kalland|first=Robby|date=April 24, 2021|title=Tobias Harris And Boban Marjanovic Talk Friendship, Basketball, John Wick 3, And More|url=https://uproxx.com/dimemag/tobias-harris-boban-marjanovic-interview-goldfish-sixers-mavs-john-wick-3/|website=Uproxx|access-date=April 24, 2021}}</ref> Marjanović and Harris appeared in a 2021 series of [[Goldfish (cracker)|Goldfish]] commercials.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Helin|first=Kurt|date=March 31, 2021|title=Tobias Harris, Boban reunite for new Goldfish commercial (VIDEO)|url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/03/31/tobias-harris-boban-reunite-for-new-goldfish-commercial-video/|website=NBC Sports|access-date=September 13, 2021}}</ref> Marjanović has also appeared in an advertising campaign for [[State Farm|State Farm Insurance]].

Marjanović appeared in [[Netflix]] film ''[[Hustle (2022 film)|Hustle]]'', produced by [[LeBron James]] and [[Adam Sandler]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bobi opet u Holivudu – u dresu Hemofarma Video|url=https://www.b92.net/sport/nba/vesti.php?yyyy=2022&mm=05&dd=11&nav_id=2152536|website=B92|date=May 11, 2022|access-date=June 28, 2026|language=sr}}</ref> He played the assassin in the 2023 comedy thriller [[Hulu]] original film ''[[Self Reliance (film)|Self Reliance]]''.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}} In the 2025 film ''[[Happy Gilmore 2]]'', Marjanović played the role of Drago Larson — a towering, deadpan enforcer hired to intimidate Happy's newest rival on the pro golf circuit.<ref>{{Cite web|title=''Happy Gilmore 2'' Cast Swings Big With Celebrity, Athlete, and Pro Golf Cameos |url=https://www.netflix.com/tudum/articles/happy-gilmore-2-cast-guide |website=Netflix|access-date=July 25, 2025}}</ref>
